# Alert

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

media and display · tier 1 · beta · renders on the server and ships no client JavaScript.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For a message that belongs to the page: a trial about to end, a failed deploy, a saved
form. Info, success, warning and danger each show their own icon, so the message reads
without relying on colour; primary and neutral take the info icon. For something that has
just happened and must be announced, use a Toast; for a bar the user can dismiss, use a
Banner.

```tsx
<Alert tone="warning" title="Your trial ends in three days">
  Deploys pause when it does. Adding a payment method turns them back on.
</Alert>

<Alert
  tone="danger"
  title="The last deploy failed"
  actions={<Button size="sm" tone="danger">Retry the deploy</Button>}
>
  The site still serves the previous version.
</Alert>
```

Alert has no role: it is page content, not a live region. Pass `role="alert"` when it is
inserted after the page has loaded and must be announced; a screen reader does not read out
an alert that is already in the first HTML. `icon={null}` hides the icon, and a long title,
description or URL wraps inside the box instead of truncating.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import { Alert } from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Every prop below is optional and falls back to the default shown.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `actions` | no | `ReactNode` | - | Buttons or links, in a row under the description. |
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The description: a sentence, several paragraphs or a list. |
| `icon` | no | `ReactNode` | - | Shown before the text. Leave it out for the tone's own icon, or pass null for none. |
| `title` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The heading of the message, in bold above the description. |
| `tone` | no | `primary` \| `neutral` \| `success` \| `warning` \| `danger` \| `info` | `"info"` | What the message means, which picks its colour ramp and its default icon. |
| `variant` | no | `soft` \| `solid` \| `outline` | `"soft"` | How much weight the alert carries on the page: a tint, a fill or an outline. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
